newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan extra budget not necessarily needed--SDP.
newsitem.headline: Japan extra budget not necessarily needed--SDP.

text.p: A supplementary budget for the current fiscal year is not necessarily needed, Kanju Sato, secretary-general of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), one of the three parties in Japan's ruling coalition, told reporters on Friday.
"There is no pressing movement to draft a supplementary budget," he said, citing worries over Japan's tight fiscal situation.
He added fears that public works spending will soon become a spent force in the economic recovery are unfounded.

He said there was much allocated public works spending from previous fiscal budgets which has not been used, and that many regional bodies will be proceeding with public works projects from this month.
"I do not agree with the idea that public works spending will run out in the second half of this fiscal year," he said.
